author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

text:
The last 20% is very hard to get AI to perfection, but what if we change the acceptance criteria, instead of asking for 1x100%, ask for 10x80% instead?
A master craftsman is better than the machines, but in the world of factory assembly line, good enough wins almost every time.
If you are a master craftsman, you don't want to be a factory worker, but becoming the factory manager maybe not too bad after all.

comments.text: I think this makes a good argument for making sure the AI generated code is still human readable and preferably with some hierarchy. It’ makes it easier for the design engineer to actually solve that lest 10 - 20% of the issues.

author.name: Bondan Rufen

comments.text: Sometimes just switching the AI model can unlock a breakthrough. Different models seem to get stuck on different problems.
